sentences.text: The instant appeal has been filed challenging the direction to pay a sum of Rs.15,00,000/- being the personal accident coverage, to the owner/driver of the insured vehicle as per the policy conditions.

2. The respondents 1 to 4 filed a claim petition stating that while the deceased was travelling in a two wheeler belonging to the fifth respondent herein, he fell down near a bridge, as a result of which he sustained fatal injuries.
3. The owner of the vehicle/fifth respondent remained ex parte before the Tribunal.

4. The appellant filed a counter stating that the deceased was the tortfeasor and in any case, the claim was not maintainable; that P.A. cover is available only to the registered owner of the vehicle holding effective licence; and therefore, the claim petition filed under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is not maintainable.
_ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5.
Before the Tribunal, the first respondent examined himself as P.W.1 and marked Exs.P1 to P9.

The appellant examined R.W1 and marked Ex.R1.
6.

The Tribunal, after taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence, held that the appellant is liable to pay personal accident cover to the extent of Rs.15,00,000/- as per the terms of policy to the deceased, who was the borrower of the vehicle and had stepped into the shoes of the owner.

7. The learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company submitted that the direction to pay the compensation at Rs.15,00,000/- in the absence of consent from the owner is erroneous; and that in any case, the appellant would not be liable to pay the interest, since the claimant could have approached the appellant directly instead of filing the petition under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988.

8. The learned counsel for the respondents 1 to 4, per contra, submitted that the claimant would be entitled to personal accident cover; _____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and fairly submitted that they may not be entitled to the interest on the said amount.
9.

The learned counsel for the fifth respondent/owner of the vehicle submitted that the deceased was the borrower of the vehicle and since he stepped into the shoes of the owner, he would be entitled to the personal accident cover.
10. The only point for consideration in the instant appeal is whether the appellant is liable to pay the compensation?
11. Admittedly, as per the terms of Ex.R1/the insurance policy, the owner-cum-driver was entitled to personal accident cover to the tune of Rs.15,00,000/-.
The fifth respondent has now admitted that the deceased was the borrower of the vehicle and therefore, had stepped into the shoes of the owner.

Therefore, the deceased would be entitled to Rs.15,00,000/- as per the judgment of the Honble Supreme Court in Ramkhiladi vs. The United India Insurance Company reported in AIR 2020 SCC M/S.Hdfc Ergo General Insurance ... vs S.Keerthiga on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173998614/
2 527.

sentences.text: _ _ _ ______ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 12.

The appellant/Insurance Company is directed to deposit a sum of Rs.15,00,000/- without interest, less the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of four (4) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
Further the direction of the tribunal to pay costs is unwarranted and hence, is set aside.
13. On such deposit, the respondents 1 and 2 shall each be entitled to Rs.6,50,000/- each and the respondents 3 and 4 shall be entitled to Rs. 1,00,000/- each.

The respondents 1, 3 and 4 are entitled to withdraw their share by filing suitable application before the Tribunal.
14.

The Tribunal is directed to deposit the share amount of the minor claimant/second respondent in any one of the Nationalized Banks in an interest bearing Fixed Deposit, initially for a period of three years, renewable thereafter, till the minor attains majority.

The guardian of the minor claimant/first respondent, who is her mother, is permitted to withdraw interest from the said deposit, once in three months and utilise the same for the welfare of the minor claimant.
__ __ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 15
. In the result, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed.
No costs.

Consequently,
connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
